hypotheses.persona: Single adult with a dog, working a flexible schedule (likely remote or hybrid). The phone leaves home around 07:00 for a morning walk (returns ~07:30-07:45) and again around 17:00 for an afternoon walk (returns ~17:45). This pattern is observed on Monday through Friday (Days 7-11) and on weekends (Days 5-6, 12-13). The earlier weekdays (Day 0, Day 4) showed a different pattern (phone gone all day), which are now the minority and likely represent occasional office days. The dog's items (blanket, ball, chew toy) are moved to the pet bed in the morning and to the sofa in the evening, confirming the dog is active. Meals are eaten at home (breakfast ~08:30, lunch ~12:30, dinner ~18:30) with dishes cleaned promptly. The phone ends up on the nightstand around 22:00-22:30, suggesting a consistent bedtime. No laptop or work bag observed yet, but the resident likely works from home on most days. — Today (Sunday) matches the weekend pattern: morning walk (06:52-07:37), afternoon walk (16:45-17:30), meals at home, dog items moved to pet bed in afternoon (ball and chew toy at 15:05) and to sofa in evening (blanket at 12:49, cushion at 16:35), phone on nightstand at 22:34. This reinforces the flexible/remote work hypothesis. The occasional office days (Day 0, Day 4) are now a small minority, so probability increased.
hypotheses.rationale: The pattern is overwhelmingly consistent with a remote worker who takes the dog out twice daily. Only 2 out of 13 days show a different pattern (phone gone all day), which could be occasional office days.

hypotheses.persona: Single adult with a dog, working a regular 9-to-5 job with occasional work-from-home. The phone leaves home around 07:00 and returns around 17:00 on some weekdays (Day 0, Day 4), consistent with a commute. However, on most observed weekdays (Days 7-11), the phone returns mid-morning and mid-afternoon, suggesting the resident is at home. This could be a hybrid schedule where the resident goes to the office on some days and works from home on others. The dog's items are moved to the pet bed in the morning and to the sofa in the evening, confirming the dog is active. Meals are eaten at home (breakfast ~08:30, lunch ~12:30, dinner ~18:30) with dishes cleaned promptly. The phone ends up on the nightstand around 22:00-22:30, suggesting a consistent bedtime. — The evidence for a regular commute is now very weak (only 2 out of 13 days). The pattern is overwhelmingly consistent with a flexible/remote worker. This hypothesis is retained only as a possible explanation for the two outlier days, but probability is reduced.
hypotheses.rationale: Only 2 out of 13 days show a full-day absence pattern, which could be occasional office days. The vast majority of days show the resident at home with dog walks.
